owasp_2021.note: Page factor table states 'CWEs Mapped 29' but the page's List of Mapped CWEs shows 30 entries; all 30 listed here as shown.

owasp_2025.name: Security Misconfiguration
owasp_2025.quote: Moving up from #5 in the previous edition, 100% of the applications tested were found to have some form of misconfiguration

owasp_2025.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
owasp_2025.covers: vulnerable/outdated components and wider supply chain (successor of A06:2021)
owasp_2025.quote: Since initially appearing in the 2013 Top 10 as "A9 – Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities", the risk has grown in scope to include all supply chain failures, not just ones involving known vulnerabilities.

owasp_2025.name: Cryptographic Failures
owasp_2025.quote: Moving down two positions to #4, this weakness focuses on failures related to the lack of cryptography, insufficiently strong cryptography, leaking of cryptographic keys, and related errors.

owasp_2025.name: Authentication Failures
owasp_2025.covers: authentication failures (was A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures)
owasp_2025.quote: Authentication Failures maintains its position at #7 with a slight name change to more accurately reflect the 36 CWEs in this category.

sp800_131a_rev2.status: Final, published 2019-03-21; still the current revision as of Oct 2026 (Rev. 3 remains an initial public draft).

currency_evidence.quote: NOTE: The initial public draft of Revision 3 (2024) is available at https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/131/a/r3/ipd. The URL for the final publication will be https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/131/a/r3/final.

sha1.digital_signature_generation: Disallowed, except where specifically allowed by NIST protocol-specific guidance

tdea_3des.quote: After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for encryption unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance.
tdea_3des.also: Same 2023 sunset for CTR_DRBG with three-key TDEA (Sec. 4 Table 3), TDEA key wrapping (Sec. 7 Table 6), CMAC-KDF with three-key TDEA (Sec. 8 Table 7).

digital_signatures.generation: Disallowed for < 112 bits (RSA len(n) < 2048; ECDSA len(n) < 224; DSA (L,N) not (2048,224),(2048,256),(3072,256))
digital_signatures.verification: Legacy use (e.g. RSA 1024 <= len(n) < 2048; ECDSA 160 <= len(n) < 224)

dh_mqv_key_agreement.status: < 112 bits of security strength: Disallowed (e.g. FFC len(p) < 2048; ECC len(n) < 224)

rsa_key_transport_agreement.quote: After December 31, 2023, the use of PKCS1-v 1_5 padding scheme is disallowed.

sp800_131a_rev3_draft.status: Initial Public Draft, 2024-10-21; comments closed 2024-12-04; not final as of 2026-10-31.

proposals.sha1_and_224bit_hashes: Deprecated through 2030; Disallowed after 2030 (for applying protection)
proposals.ecb: Disallowed for encrypting secret data; legacy use only
proposals.dsa: Signature generation Disallowed; verification Legacy use

sp800_131a_rev3_draft.quote: TDEA is disallowed as of 2024 (see Sec. 2). This revision of SP 800-131A also deprecates SHA-1 and the 224-bit hash functions through December 31, 2030, and disallows them thereafter for applying cryptographic protection

ir8547.status: Final, October 2026 (CSRC lists final 2026-10-27; approved by NIST ERB 2026-10-21); draft (ipd) was 2024-11-12.
ir8547.quote: NIST will deprecate quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography after 2030 and disallow its use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.

change_from_draft.detail: The Nov 2024 draft split rows: 112-bit = 'Deprecated after 2030, Disallowed after 2035'; >=128-bit = 'Disallowed after 2035' only. The final collapses to a single row (>=112 bits, or >=128 for EdDSA): deprecated after 2030 for all strengths.

federal_accelerators.quote: These systems must adopt post-quantum cryptography for key establishment by December 31, 2030, and for digital signatures by December 31, 2031.
federal_accelerators.context: EO 14412 / OMB M-26-15, high value assets and high impact systems; TLS 1.3 support required no later than January 2, 2030 (EO 14306 / OMB M-26-15).

sha1_footnote.quote: The SHA-1 hash function is currently deprecated for all remaining technical applications and will be disallowed for use in FIPS-validated cryptographic modules after 2030.

symmetric_112.quote: NIST has a few symmetric cryptography standards at the 112-bit security level, which will be disallowed in 2030.

ir8547.ml_kem_default: NIST recommends using ML-KEM-768 as the default parameter set

cbom_definition.quote: The CBOM is an inventory of cryptographic assets—including algorithms, keys, protocols, certificates, and dependencies—capturing critical metadata such as usage patterns and expiration dates.

minimum_elements_table9.section: 8.3, Table 9 'Minimum Elements pertaining to Cryptographic Asset', pp.45-48
minimum_elements_table9.note: Table 8 (QBOM, p.44) says: 'For a cryptographic asset, the minimum elements that are to be included in the QBOM are mentioned in table 9 depending on the cryptographic asset type.'

key_recommendations.8.4.1.1: All government, public sector, and essential services organizations shall require a comprehensive Bill of Materials (BOM), specifically a Cryptographic BOM (CBOM) for cryptographic assets and a Quantum BOM (QBOM) for quantum systems in all related procurements, developments, and integrations.
key_recommendations.8.4.1.5: BOMs shall be generated using recognized industry-standard formats, such as Software Package Data eXchange (SPDX) or CycloneDX
key_recommendations.8.4.1.6: VEX with status Not Affected / Affected / Fixed / Under Investigation
key_recommendations.8.4.2.2: Enforce strict TLS configurations by specifying approved cipher suites, certificate chains, and session parameters, and prohibit the use of weak or deprecated algorithms.
key_recommendations.8.4.2.8: Conduct scheduled reviews, at least quarterly, to verify accuracy and completeness.
key_recommendations.8.5.1: Public key systems using RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman, and DSA algorithms are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm

directions_2022.crypto_content: None. Text contains no encryption/TLS/cryptography requirement; it covers NTP sync, 6-hour incident reporting, 180-day log retention, etc.

govt_entities_guidelines.title: Guidelines on Information Security Practices for Government Entities
govt_entities_guidelines.date: June 2023 (PDF creation date 2023-06-23; no date printed in text)

clauses.4.5.7 (pg.12): use secure protocols such as SSH, SSL, or IP Security (IPSec) encryption for all remote connections to the router/switch/server.
clauses.4.10.2 (pg.15): secured using highest graded encryption (WPA-2 or higher) for data confidentiality and integrity.
clauses.6.1.7 (pg.21): Ensure that all Websites and Applications are "https" enabled with a valid SSL/TLS Certificate.
clauses.6.2.2 (pg.21): The mobile application must implement SSL Pinning to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.
clauses.6.2.7 (pg.22): Sensitive data should be shared over secure SSL/TLS connection only.
clauses.7.1 (pg.22): Identify and classify sensitive/personal data and apply measures for encrypting such data in transit and at rest.

inequality.quote: If TSHELF-LIFE + TMIGRATION > TTHREAT, that is, if the time required to migrate the system plus the time for which the information needs to be protected goes beyond the time ...

definitions.X_shelf_life: the number of years the information should be protected for
definitions.Y_migration: the number of years needed to safely and adequately migrate the cyber-system to a quantum-safe solution
definitions.Z_threat: the number of years before the relevant threat actors will be able to break the quantum-vulnerable systems, an event often referred to as "Q-Day"
